乌云沉甸甸压在天际，湿冷的土腥味扑面而来。
远处天际隐隐滚过闷雷，一场倾盆大雨随时都会砸落。
陈越提着鸡笼，深一脚浅一脚地踩在泥泞小路上，额角的冷汗混着潮气往下淌，后背早已被汗湿的衣衫贴得难受。
他本是现代一个普通人，一天晚上闭眼入睡，再睁眼竟魂穿到了这个酷似华夏古代的陌生世界，成了县城里一家药铺的学徒。
说是学徒，实则比府里的下人还要卑微，每日干的都是劈柴、挑水、跑腿的粗活，正经药理医术半点没学到手。
前些日子又无意间冲撞了药铺里的管事，如今便被随意指派了这般苦差事。
去荒郊乡下收公鸡，美其名曰“入药需鲜活土鸡”，可陈越心里清楚，不过是故意刁难。
县城里随处可买的公鸡，何必特意跑这么远来收？陈越想过偷偷在县里买，但看那管事的眼神，他似乎就等着陈越这样做。
来回几十里土路，偏偏还赶上了这要命的暴雨天。
公鸡被狂风惊得焦躁不安，时不时扑腾着挣扎，陈越提得手腕发酸，抬眼望见不远处林间露出一截破败的庙檐，知道再耽搁下去，怕是要被暴雨淋成一场大病。
真生大病了，就学徒的身份，能不能扛过去，就真看命了。
想到这，陈越索性提着鸡笼，快步冲进了那座荒弃已久的破庙。
庙门早已朽坏，半敞着露出漆黑的庙内，神像断首残臂，周身落满厚厚的灰尘与蛛网，墙角堆着干枯的柴草，满地碎石瓦砾，透着一股久无人烟的阴冷死寂。
陈越反手将歪扭的庙门掩上大半，先把鸡笼放到墙角，随即捡来干燥柴草，借着随身携带的火石，费劲地点起一团篝火。
橙红色的火苗蹿起，驱散了几分周身的湿冷，也将庙内的阴暗撕开一道小口。
火光摇曳不定，映得残破神像的虚影在土墙上忽明忽暗，时而狰狞扭曲，时而沉寂诡异，看得人心里发毛。
陈越凑近火堆，烘干身上半湿的衣衫，从怀里掏出硬邦邦的干粮，就着腰间水囊里的冷水小口啃食。
风越发狂躁，拍打着朽坏的庙门发出呜呜声响，闷雷越来越近，震得庙顶尘土簌簌掉落。
就在陈越咽下最后一口干粮时，一道刺目的白光骤然划破天际，紧接着震耳欲聋的惊雷在头顶炸开，震得人耳膜发疼，下一秒，密集的雨点轰然砸落。

笃、笃、笃！
惊雷余音未散，庙门外竟突兀响起了一阵敲门声。
声响不重，却在这荒庙死寂里显得格外刺耳。陈越浑身肌肉瞬间紧绷，下意识伸手抓过身旁劈柴用的柴刀。
陈越没应声，门外的人却没耐心等待，朽坏的庙门被缓缓推开一道缝隙，雨水顺着门缝灌进来，带着刺骨的寒意。
来人身穿蓑衣，头戴斗笠，背着一个竹编的药篓，像是个采药人。他看到陈越和地上的火堆，斗笠下的脸上露出欣喜之色。
“这位小兄弟，雨太大了，还好这里有火，能否借个地方烤烤？”
采药人声音沙哑，边说边摘下斗笠，露出一张中年人的脸，面色黝黑，眼角有着深深的皱纹。
他卸下药篓，里面装着些常见的草药。
话音刚落，墙角鸡笼里的公鸡像是被刚才的惊雷彻底吓破了胆，原本只是时不时扑腾，此刻突然疯狂挣扎起来，拼了命地撞鸡笼。
陈越看着眼前的采药人，从上到下快速打量一番，神情憨厚老实。
沉默片刻，陈越缓缓点头，上前一步将半开的庙门彻底关上，关门的前一秒，他抬眼扫向庙外。
暴雨如注，天地间一片白茫茫，除了肆虐的风雨，看不到半个人影。地面上，除了陈越之前的脚印，没有其他多的。
采药人道谢后，便坐到火堆另一侧，伸出冻得冰凉的手凑近火苗，静静地烤了片刻火。
庙内只剩下风雨声、柴火燃烧的噼啪声，还有公鸡拼命扑腾的声音，气氛沉闷得让人喘不过气。
“小兄弟是附近的人？”采药人搓着手道。
“路过。”陈越简短回答。
“我是进山采药的，没想到遇到大雨，还好有这座庙。”
采药人从怀里掏出一个干粮袋，也拿出饼子啃起来，“长夜漫漫，不如我讲个故事解解闷如何？”
采药人抬眼看向陈越，嘴角噙着一抹淡笑，火光落在他脸上，明暗交错，看不清眼底的情绪。

Dark clouds were heavy in the sky, and the smell of cold, wet earth hit my face.
Muffled thunder rolled faintly across the sky in the distance, and a heavy downpour could fall at any time.
Chen Yue carried the chicken coop and stepped heavily on the muddy path. Cold sweat mixed with moisture dripped down his forehead, and his back was already uncomfortable with sweat-soaked clothes.
He was an ordinary person in modern times. One night he closed his eyes and fell asleep. When he opened his eyes again, he was transported to this strange world that resembled ancient China and became an apprentice in a drug store in the county.
He was said to be an apprentice, but in fact he was even humbler than the servants in the mansion. Every day he had to do menial tasks such as chopping firewood, carrying water, and running errands, and he had not learned any serious pharmacological and medical skills.
A few days ago, I accidentally bumped into the manager of the drug store, and now I was randomly assigned to such a hard job.
Going to the deserted countryside to collect roosters, euphemistically calling it "fresh local chickens are needed for medicine", but Chen Yue knew in his heart that he was just deliberately making things difficult.
Why go all the way to collect roosters when you can buy them everywhere in the county? Chen Yue thought about buying it secretly in the county, but looking at the look in the manager's eyes, he seemed to be waiting for Chen Yue to do this.
After going back and forth for dozens of miles on a dirt road, we happened to catch up with this terrible rainstorm.
The rooster was frightened by the strong wind and was flapping and struggling from time to time. Chen Yue's wrists were sore from raising his eyes. He looked up and saw a dilapidated temple eaves exposed in the forest not far away. He knew that if he delayed any longer, he might become seriously ill due to the heavy rain.
If you really get seriously ill, as an apprentice, it really depends on your fate whether you can survive it.
Thinking of this, Chen Yue simply carried the chicken coop and quickly rushed into the ruined temple that had been abandoned for a long time.
The temple door has long since decayed, and is half-open to reveal the dark interior of the temple. The statue of the god has its head and arms broken off, and its whole body is covered with thick dust and cobwebs. There are dried firewood piled in the corner of the wall, and the ground is covered with gravel and rubble. There is a cold and dead silence that has been uninhabited for a long time.
Chen Yue closed most of the crooked temple door with his backhand, first put the chicken coop in the corner, then picked up dry firewood, and struggled to light a bonfire with the flint he brought with him.
Orange-red flames jumped up, dispelling some of the dampness and coldness around him, and also tore a small hole in the darkness in the temple.
The light of the fire wavered uncertainly, making the shadow of the broken statue flicker on the earthen wall. Sometimes it looked ferocious and twisted, sometimes it was silent and strange, which made people's hearts tremble.
Chen Yue approached the fire, dried his half-wet clothes, took out hard dry food from his arms, and nibbled on the cold water in the water bag around his waist.
The wind became more and more violent, beating against the decaying temple door and making a whining sound. The muffled thunder got closer and closer, shaking the dust from the top of the temple.
Just when Chen Yue swallowed his last mouthful of dry food, a dazzling white light suddenly pierced the sky, and then deafening thunder exploded above his head, making people's eardrums hurt. The next second, dense raindrops crashed down.
Tuk, Tuk, Tuk!
Before the sound of thunder dissipated, a knock on the door suddenly sounded outside the temple door.
The sound was not loud, but it was particularly harsh in the dead silence of this deserted temple. Chen Yue's muscles tightened instantly, and he subconsciously reached out to grab the hatchet used to chop wood next to him.
Chen Yue didn't answer, but the people outside the door didn't wait patiently. The decaying temple door was slowly pushed open a crack, and rainwater poured in along the crack of the door, bringing a biting chill.
The person who came was wearing a raincoat and a bamboo hat, carrying a bamboo medicine basket on his back, like a medicine gatherer. He saw Chen Yue and the fire on the ground, and his face under the bamboo hat showed a look of joy.
"Little brother, it's raining too much. Fortunately, there is a fire here. Can you borrow a place to bake?"
The herb collector's voice was hoarse. As he spoke, he took off his hat, revealing a middle-aged face with dark complexion and deep wrinkles at the corners of his eyes.
He unloaded the medicine basket, which contained some common herbs.
As soon as he finished speaking, the rooster in the chicken coop in the corner seemed to be completely frightened by the thunder just now. It was just fluttering from time to time, but now it suddenly started struggling crazily and hit the chicken coop with all its strength.
Chen Yue looked at the herb picker in front of him and quickly looked at him from top to bottom.Love is simple and honest.
After a moment of silence, Chen Yue nodded slowly, stepped forward and closed the half-open temple door completely. The second before closing the door, he raised his eyes and glanced outside the temple.
There was a heavy rain, and the sky and the earth were completely white. Apart from the raging wind and rain, not a single person could be seen. On the ground, apart from Chen Yue's previous footprints, there were not many others.
After the herb gatherer thanked him, he sat on the other side of the fire, stretched out his cold hands to the flames, and quietly warmed himself for a while.
The only sounds left in the temple were the sound of wind and rain, the crackle of burning firewood, and the sound of roosters flapping desperately. The atmosphere was so dull that people could not breathe.
"Is this little brother from around here?" the herb collector said while rubbing his hands.
"Passing by." Chen Yue replied briefly.
"I went into the mountains to collect herbs. I didn't expect to encounter heavy rain. Fortunately, there is this temple."
The herb gatherer took out a dry food bag from his arms, and also took out the pancakes and gnawed on them, "It's a long night, how about I tell a story to relieve the boredom?"
The herb collector looked up at Chen Yue, with a faint smile on his lips. The firelight fell on his face, with light and dark intertwined, making it difficult to see the emotions in his eyes.
